Meta.title: Phronesis — Practical wisdom for AI agent systems
Meta.description: Phronesis is an open source Python framework for building AI agent systems with typed contracts, composable execution patterns, and observability built in.
Meta.ogDescription: Open source Python framework for AI agent systems. Typed contracts, composable pipelines, observability built in.

Hero.heading: Practical wisdom for AI agent systems.
Hero.leadMiddle: — the capacity to deliberate well and act with judgment in concrete situations. An LLM has

Why.heading: An agent is not a chatbot with tools.
Why.p1AfterStrong: with judgment in concrete situations. That is
Why.p1End: . Most agent frameworks treat agents as enhanced chatbots glued to a tool-use loop. Phronesis treats them as deliberating systems with explicit contracts: typed inputs, declared effects, bounded memory, named execution patterns.
Why.p2Before: Existing frameworks force a choice. On one side, you write arbitrary control flow as code: maximal expressiveness, and a multi-agent system that nobody can debug six months later. On the other, everything is described in YAML or graph-builders: legible at a glance, impossible the moment you need something non-trivial. Phronesis separates declarative specification from runtime execution. Agents, tools, memory, pipelines are
Why.p2End: . Execution patterns come from a closed, well-defined catalog — expressiveness without chaos.
Why.p3: Every run is observable through OpenTelemetry, every spec is versionable, every contract is a runtime check, not a comment in a prompt. This is the difference between a framework that produces demos and one that produces systems you can operate.

CodeTour.heading: The API in four snippets.
CodeTour.intro: Real Python. Real shape. The framework you see below is in early alpha — the surface area will grow, but the design will stay this lean.

agent.label: Agent
agent.description: An agent binds a model, tools, and memory under a single declarative spec.

tool.label: Tool
tool.description: Tools are typed contracts. Effects are declared so the runtime can reason about safety.

pipeline.label: Pipeline
pipeline.description: Pipelines compose stages. Each stage runs in one of a closed catalog of execution modes.

mcp.label: MCP
mcp.description: Attach MCP servers as first-class tool sources, with the same safety contracts as native tools.

Patterns.heading: Designed for the agent shapes that recur.
Patterns.intro: These are patterns the framework supports today. They are not case studies — we have no production users to claim yet, and we will not pretend otherwise.

research.title: Research agents
research.description: Agents that gather information, reason over it, and synthesize answers with citations.

document.title: Document agents
document.description: Agents that read, structure, and act on documents with explicit memory of what they have seen.

multiAgent.title: Multi-agent pipelines
multiAgent.description: Pipelines composing specialized agents through handoffs, debate, or consensus.

toolUsing.title: Tool-using assistants
toolUsing.description: Agents that invoke typed tools and MCP servers under explicit safety contracts.

composition.title: Composition over inheritance
composition.body: Agents are configured from parts — model, tools, memory, prompts — not subclassed. You assemble; you don't override.

async.title: Async-first
async.body: Streaming, concurrency, and cancellation are baseline assumptions. There is no synchronous shadow API to maintain.

typed.title: Strongly typed
typed.body: Pydantic v2 throughout. Types are not documentation — they are runtime contracts the framework enforces.

immutable.title: Immutable specs, mutable runs
immutable.body: Definitions are JSON-serializable and reproducible. Execution state lives apart, observable and queryable.

observable.title: Observability built in
observable.body: OpenTelemetry spans for every agent run, tool call, and pipeline stage — from the first commit, not bolted on.

catalog.title: Closed catalog of execution patterns
catalog.body: Sequence, Parallel, ReActLoop, Consensus, Debate, Handoff. Named modes you can reason about — not arbitrary control flow.

Inside.heading: A small, principled surface.
Inside.intro: The framework is intentionally narrow. Each layer earns its place by either making a system safer to operate or making the code simpler to read six months later.

core.title: Core
core.description: The primitives every agent is built from.

state.title: State and context
state.description: How agents remember and what they share.

Inside.executionModesNote: A closed catalog — expressive enough, finite enough to reason about.

Status.heading: Phronesis is in early alpha.
Status.p1: The API will change. We are working in public to build a framework that takes agent systems seriously — typed, composable, observable. No production claims, no fabricated case studies, no enterprise gates. Just the code, and an honest commitment to its design.
Status.p2: Feedback, ideas, and contributions are welcome through GitHub Discussions and Issues. The roadmap, the rough edges, and the open questions are all in the repository.
